Bit-perfect means the audio reaches the DAC exactly as it is in the file, bit for bit. Normally Android sends all sound through its mixer, which can change the sample rate (for example, to 48 kHz), adjust the volume digitally and mix it with other system sounds. In bit-perfect mode the mixer is bypassed and the DAC receives the original data, at its own sample rate and bit depth.

Android added [official support](https://source.android.com/docs/core/audio/preferred-mixer-attr) in Android 14, with the AudioMixerAttributes API and the MIXER_BEHAVIOR_BIT_PERFECT mode, only for USB DACs. However, having Android 14 is not enough: the manufacturer must enable it in the phone\'s audio configuration, and the music app must request it. Before Android 14, only some apps achieved it by using their own proprietary USB driver (e.g. USB Audio Player Pro, FiiO Music, HiBy Music, among others).
It helps audiophiles to identify if their current phone has native bit-perfect support.

Without a DAC connected, the app reads the audio configuration the manufacturer installed on the phone. \"According to the manufacturer\" means the phone declares it; when you connect a USB DAC, Android confirms it definitively.
With a DAC connected, results come directly from Android (AudioManager.getSupportedMixerAttributes).
